html:
Abu al-Qasim al-Shabbi was a Tunisian poet who died of heart disease at 25 in 1934, and is remembered as the national poet of Tunisia. He was born near Tozeur and studied at the Zaytuna in Tunis.

He wrote romantic poems about nature, love and freedom, in a new style that broke with the old forms of Arabic verse. His poem The Will to Life begins: if the people one day want to live, fate must answer.

Its last lines were added to Tunisia's national anthem. In 2011 they were chanted in the streets during the Tunisian revolution and across the Arab Spring, from Cairo to Sana'a. See also Tunisia.
